text:
cheng: quick brain dump  I experimented with replacing our per-page prefetch bitmap with a compact 'tilemap' that coalesces contiguous GPU-backed ranges into tiles. high-level goal: cut metadata pressure and reduce tiny pinned fragments when migrating hot slices. tradeoffs below.

maria: ok curious  show the design sketch

cheng: sketch: maintain a sorted vector/list of tiles (start_page, page_len, hot_score). tiles merge if adjacent and same residency. prefetch chooses whole tiles, not individual pages. membership test via binary search on vector. updates touch only affected shards. wins: far fewer metadata entries and better coalesce on evict/restore.

ajay: what about partial residency (tile only partially resident)?

cheng: two options: (1) split-on-write: break tile when a subset changes; or (2) keep an in-tile submask (e.g., 64-bit) to represent subpage state. the prototype uses split-on-write to keep fast path simple; we can add submask later to reduce splits for small partials.

samir: split-on-write might cause metadata churn for models with many small attention accesses. do you have numbers?

cheng: quick run: baseline page map ~2.8M entries for ~40GB working set. tilemap with avg tile=4 pages -> ~720k tiles. update ops down ~3.5x. split operations increased ~1.4x on tiny-random synthetic traces.

maria: interaction with KV cache and batching? bigger prefetches can increase cold KV pulls and waste CPU/GPU bandwidth.

cheng: yeah. we weight tile hot_score by access density; low-density tiles deprioritized. we also cap prefetch bytes per request (config: tile_prefetch_bytes_limit) to bound amplification.

ajay: who owns the tilemap? per-tenant logical map, per-GPU residency view, global?

cheng: proposal: per-tenant logical tilemap (sharded by hotset hash) + per-GPU residency bitset/view. sync deltas across nodes to avoid global locks. infra-bot: deploy-ci: check that diffs fit current delta-sync (max 64KB/heartbeat).

samir: fairness concerns: one tenant could pin a massive tile and hoard GPU pages.

cheng: mitigations: soft caps (max_tiles_per_tenant_active), an eviction-split heuristic that prefers splitting large low-hot-score tiles first, plus existing tenant slot-level quotas.

maria: telemetry/API changes? teams rely on per-page counters today.

ajay: add a temporary shim that exposes per-page-like counters for 3 months. we should emit new counters too: tile_count, avg_tile_size, tile_split_events, tile_prefetch_bytes.

cheng: proto sketch in prototype: 
```
// Tile proto (pseudocode)
struct Tile { uint64 start_page; uint32 page_len; float hot_score; uint64 submask64; // optional
};
// merge rule
if (adjacent(a,b) && same_state(a,b) && combined_len <= MAX_TILE_PAGES) merge(a,b);
```

samir: concurrency/race windows: merging needs atomic ops across shard lists. we must avoid blocking hot allocation paths.

cheng: implemented non-blocking background coalescer that snapshots shard (RCU-like), compacts vector, and swaps in new vector. hot path has optimistic try-merge fastpath using CAS, otherwise enqueue to coalescer.

maria: any perf regressions on small-batch latencies (99th)?

cheng: microbench results: 99th latency +5% for tiny inferences (binary search overhead); throughput +8%; memory metadata overhead -12%. seems tradeoff-y. gate behind runtime feature flag.

ajay: rollout plan: canary on Dedicated pool with single-tenant hosts, watch metrics for 48h. revert if tile_split_per_min > threshold or 99th latency regresses too much.

samir: also surface avg_tile_size per tenant in SRE dashboards to catch hoarding.

cheng: plan: open PR with proto + shim + runtime flag + background coalescer. create canary job config and grafana dashboard panels. link when ready.

maria: :thumbsup: happy to help build dashboard panels.

infra-bot: deploy-notice: created canary pool 'tilemap-canary' (3 hosts)  include feature-flag header on requests.

cheng: thanks all  will post PR and perf dumps.
